title: Rerunning the Bubble-Sort Debate: Two AI audits of the Dietz and Sweet articles on Zhang, Goldstein & Levin's self-sorting arrays
description:
Two separately run, machine-checkable audits of the mathematics, code, citations and quotations in Joel Dietz's Why Michael Levin Is 77.6++% Right on Platonic Ingress (text supplied 2026-11-01; public draft in fractastical/morpholib @ 35d30f4) and Nathan Sweet's Why Michael Levin's Bubble Sort “Revelation” Is Misunderstood (revised 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-31), with a cross-audit article, Rerunning the Bubble-Sort Debate (CROSS_AUDIT.md).

Contents: runs of the original threaded code of Zhang, Goldstein & Levin (2025) at commit 1fd2bd5; exact combinatorics in Python and Node.js; Lean 4 proofs; replays of Dietz's sequential model at morpholib bfe377c and 35d30f4; DOI resolution of every cited reference; quotation checks against pinned sources; FishShapes and wing-data rebuilds; nanopublication signature checks; claim ledgers; SHA-256 manifests; a GitHub Actions workflow that reruns the deterministic checks.

The audits were performed with AI coding agents (Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Cowork; OpenAI Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol, as reported by the author), which are tools, not authors. Agreement between them is not independent scientific replication. Third-party full texts and unlicensed upstream code are not redistributed; each removal is listed with its SHA-256.
